$comment: ONE replaceAllText request through v1/presentations/{presentationId}:batchUpdate: every occurrence of a string, replaced, across the whole presentation. ReplaceAllTextRequest {containsText: SubstringMatchCriteria {text, matchCase}, replaceText, pageObjectIds}; the reply is ReplaceAllTextResponse {occurrencesChanged}. Read from Google's discovery document 2026-11-08. The template-filling case: {{name}} -> a value.
title: Replace text in a Google Slides presentation
description: Replace every occurrence of a string in a presentation.
$idempotencyComment: A retry is a no-op only when the replacement does not itself contain the searched text; when it does, a retry replaces again.

config.label: Presentation ID
config.description: From presentation_create's data.presentationId, or the id in the presentation's own URL.

config.label: Find
config.description: The exact text to find, e.g. {{name}}. Not a regular expression.

config.label: Replace with
config.description: Inserted in place of every match. Empty is refused: to delete text, use batch_update.

config.label: Match case
config.description: Off matches case-insensitively, which is also what Google does when it is not sent.

config.label: Only on slides
config.description: Optional. Slide objectIds, comma separated (from presentation_get). Empty means every slide.

config.label: Required revision ID
config.description: Optional. The presentation's revisionId as you last read it. If the presentation has changed since, Google refuses the whole batch with a 400 instead of applying it to content you have not seen.

outputShape.description: How many occurrences were replaced. 0 means the text was not found, which is not an error.
The presentation's revision after the update.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
